minutes.headline: Commission agreed to oppose Article 24, a Town Meeting appeal of APDC demolition denials for town buildings.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met remotely and discussed Warrant Article 24, which would let a party aggrieved by an APDC denial of a demolition certificate for town property appeal to Town Meeting. This is widely seen as aimed at the old primary school. A member read lengthy remarks against it, members agreed on a position, and one member will write it up for Town Meeting. They also discussed a National Register nomination for the old primary school and checked whether the Ritter building is listed.

public_comment.topic: Said the Select Board chair plans to amend Article 24 to limit it to the town, called it a bad article, and criticised the TC Passios plan, suggesting the Brooks House could house school offices.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said they had read that money would be found to upgrade the building; another said it is yet to be seen whether the town will spend it.

budget_items.topic: TC Passios renovation cost per square foot
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident gave the building size and a per-square-foot renovation price and questioned whether the space was needed.

why_it_matters: Article 24 is a Town Meeting vote on whether the commission's power to deny demolition of town-owned buildings can be appealed to Town Meeting, and the old primary school is widely seen as the building at issue.
A National Register nomination for the old primary school is being prepared, which could bear on any later decision about that building.
watch_next: The commission's written position on Article 24, to be prepared for Town Meeting.
Whether Article 24 is amended to limit it to the town, as a resident said is planned.
